items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Compare the dates. The first sentence is set in 2019, and the blank sentence goes back to 1987 to describe the marsh before its decline. A backward jump in time calls for 'Previously.'

A.why: You assumed the text keeps moving forward because the 1987 sentence comes second. 'Subsequently' points later in time, but 1987 is earlier than 2019.

C.why: You picked a cause word because the two sentences sit next to each other. The 2019 count did not cause the 1987 count. The earlier count is background, not a result.

D.why: You treated the sentences as similar. Sixty pairs and fourteen pairs are not alike. The blank sentence gives an earlier point in time, not a matching example.

items.stimulus: Around 1650, many European maps of North America showed California as a large island, separated from the mainland by a long, narrow sea. ______ explorers who traveled overland around the head of that sea reported that California was joined to the continent, and mapmakers redrew the coastline to match.

items.subtype_name: Timeline and steps (Earlier / Previously / Later / Eventually)
items.stimulus: In 1994, a park ranger exploring a narrow canyon near Sydney, Australia, came upon a small stand of unfamiliar conifers, now called Wollemi pines. ______, scientists had known this lineage of trees only from fossilized leaves and pollen, some of them roughly 90 million years old.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Before you look at the choices, date each sentence. The first sentence is set in 1994, when the living trees were found. The second sentence says scientists 'had known' the trees only from fossils. The verb 'had known' points to a time before 1994. That means the blank sentence goes back in time to give background, so you need a word that looks backward, and 'Previously' is the one that does. This is the basic step in every timeline transition question: compare the dates themselves, not the order the sentences appear in. Once you can do this on two sentences, you can do it in a full SAT passage with more dates and more distractors.

B.why: You assumed the passage keeps moving forward because the second sentence comes after the first. But knowing the trees only from fossils happened before the 1994 discovery, not after it. Once living trees had been found, scientists no longer knew them only from fossils, so 'Later' reverses the real order of events. This is the trap this question type is built to catch: following the order of the sentences instead of the dates.

C.why: You picked a cause word because one event is mentioned right after the other. The 1994 discovery didn't cause scientists to know the trees only from fossils. That situation existed before the discovery and ended because of it. Coming next in the text does not make something an effect.

D.why: 'For example' introduces one member of a larger group named in the sentence before it. The first sentence names no group of things to sample from. It describes one discovery. The second sentence doesn't illustrate that discovery. It tells you what was known before it, which is a time relationship, not an example.

items.stimulus: By the 1850s, a single weaver tending four power looms in a Lancashire cotton mill could turn out several times as much cloth in a day as a hand weaver working alone. The gap between the two methods had not always been so wide. ______ in the 1810s, the first power looms had barely outpaced a skilled hand weaver, and frequent breakdowns of their wooden frames often wiped out even that small lead.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Put a date on each sentence. The first sentence is set in the 1850s. The sentence with the blank is set in the 1810s, about forty years before. The sentence just before the blank also tells you the gap 'had not always been so wide,' which means the text is about to go back in time to show the gap when it was small. A transition that moves backward is needed, and 'Earlier' is the one that does that.

A.why: You assumed the passage keeps moving forward because the blank comes later in the paragraph. Look at the dates: the 1810s come before the 1850s, so the blank sentence goes back in time instead of forward.

C.why: You read the order of events as cause and effect. Weak early looms in the 1810s are not a result of the productive looms of the 1850s. The two sentences are linked by time, not by cause.

D.why: 'Finally' marks the last step in a sequence or the end point of a process. The 1810s are the starting point of the story, not its end, so this points the wrong way along the timeline.

items.subtype_name: Timeline and steps (Earlier / Previously / Later / Eventually)
items.stimulus: To measure the effects of a city's 2016 minimum wage increase, economist Lena Okafor followed a two-stage plan. She first gathered payroll records for workers aged 16 to 19 from 2014 and 2015, which gave her a baseline from before the increase. ______ she collected the same records for 2017 and 2018. Compared with the baseline, teen hourly earnings had risen by 9 percent, while teen hours worked had fallen by only 3 percent.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The passage sets out a two-stage plan, and the word 'first' marks stage one: records from 2014 and 2015. The blank sentence is stage two, with records from 2017 and 2018, which come after the baseline years. So you need a transition that moves forward to the next step. 'Subsequently' means 'after that,' which is exactly that relationship.

A.why: 'Previously' sends the reader back in time. The blank sentence covers 2017 and 2018, which come after the 2014–2015 baseline, and it is the second stage of the plan, not something done before the first.

B.why: 'For instance' introduces one example from a larger group. Collecting the later records is not an example of collecting the baseline records. It is the next step in the plan.

C.why: You picked a cause word just because one step came after the other. Gathering the baseline did not cause Okafor to collect later records. The plan called for both stages, so the link is sequence, not cause.

items.subtype_name: Timeline and steps (Earlier / Previously / Later / Eventually)
items.stimulus: In 1912, biochemist Casimir Funk proposed the name "vitamine," from "vital amine," for the trace dietary factors whose absence caused diseases such as beriberi. Over the following years, however, researchers isolated more of these factors, and many turned out to contain no amines at all. ______ in 1920, biochemist Jack Drummond recommended dropping the final "e," and the shortened word "vitamin" was soon widely adopted.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Track the timeline. Funk's name comes in 1912. Discoveries pile up 'over the following years.' The blank sentence lands in 1920, eight years after Funk's proposal, and describes how the naming problem was settled in the end. A transition that marks the outcome of a long process is needed, and 'Eventually' does that.

A.why: 'Previously' looks backward, but 1920 comes after both 1912 and the years of discovery that followed. Compare the dates themselves: the blank sentence moves forward to the end of the story.

C.why: 'Similarly' adds a point that matches the one before it. Drummond's proposal is not a parallel to the discovery of amine-free factors. It is the later response that solved the problem those discoveries created.

D.why: 'For example' introduces one member of a larger group. Drummond's 1920 recommendation is not an example of researchers isolating new factors. It is the step that ended the sequence.
